facts.fact_text: In May 2005, after the applicant had been released from detention but while the criminal case against her was still pending, the applicant and two others, Ms I. and Ms B., decided to stage a static demonstration (пикетирование) in front of various public authorities in Moscow, including the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation.
The purpose of the static demonstration planned by the applicant, Ms I. and Ms B. was to protest against the allegedly unlawful actions of public authorities and corruption.

According to the applicant, the demonstration related to persistent difficulties in relation to pending cases involving law enforcement agencies and courts, in particular in the Irkutsk Region, and the failure of the local authorities to deal with their grievances.
On 7 June 2005 at 9.30 a.m., the applicant and her friends Ms I. and Ms B. placed themselves on a pavement separated from the building of the Federal Judges Qualifications Board by a road.
On 7 June 2005, the police officer told the applicant and her friends to cease their demonstration and follow him to the police station.
The police officer compelled the applicant and her friends to follow him to the police station.
The Justice of the Peace found the applicant guilty of non-compliance with a lawful order by a police officer, an offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Justice of the Peace sentenced the applicant to seven days of detention, to be counted from the moment of her arrest on the morning of 7 June 2005.
The applicant was released on 14 June 2005, having served the sentence imposed by the Justice of the Peace.

Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that non-compliance with a lawful order by a police officer, given within the scope of his or her professional duties, is punishable by a fine or administrative detention of up to fifteen days.

Article 20.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences provided that violation of the rules or procedure for organising or participating in a public gathering (a meeting, demonstration or static demonstration) is punishable by a fine.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found on 27 June 2005 that the applicant refused to comply with lawful orders to end the violation of the public order and threatened police officers with prosecution, thereby resisting a lawful order by police officers.
The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow noted on 27 June 2005 that section 8 of the Public Gatherings Act prohibits public events in the immediate vicinity of court buildings.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow noted on 27 June 2005 that section 17 of the Public Gatherings Act provides that failure to comply with a lawful order of the police or resistance to the police entails the liability of the persons concerned.
On 30 May 2005, the applicant, Ms I. and Ms B. sent a telegram to the Moscow Mayor's Office informing the authorities of their intention to stage static demonstrations between 3 and 16 June 2005.
On 31 May 2005, the Moscow Mayor's Office acknowledged receipt of the telegram sent by the applicant, Ms I. and Ms B. on 30 May 2005.

The applicant explained to the police officer that they needed no authorisation and produced the telegram message sent to the Moscow Mayor's Office and the certified copy of the telegram bearing the mayor's office stamp.

The applicant's written statement at the police station stated that she was holding a static demonstration at 9.45 a.m. on 7 June 2005 in conformity with the Public Gatherings Act, as notified to the authorities on 30 May 2005.

Section 7(1) of the Public Gatherings Act (Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004) provided that for a static demonstration by several people notification may be made no later than three days before the demonstration.

Section 12(1) of the Public Gatherings Act (Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004) provided that the competent public authority should acknowledge in writing receipt of the notification and indicate the date and time of receipt.

Section 12(1) of the Public Gatherings Act (Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004) provided that the competent public authority should inform the event organiser on the same day — in the case of a notification received less than five days before a static demonstration by several people — of any alternative proposal concerning the event venue and/or time.
Section 8 of the Public Gatherings Act (Federal Law no. 54-FZ of 19 June 2004) provided that no public event could be held in the immediate vicinity of court buildings.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found on 27 June 2005 that on 7 June 2005 the applicant held a non-authorised demonstration and held a banner containing a very negative assessment of the professional activity of the Prosecutor General, the President of the Supreme Court and the Minister of Justice.
On 1 July 2005, the Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow examined Ms I.'s appeal and discontinued the administrative offence case against her.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found on 1 July 2005 that the administrative offence record against Ms I. contained no indication of the content of the repeated orders of the police officers.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found on 1 July 2005 that the administrative proceedings against Ms I. were initiated in relation to a fact falling within the scope of Article 20.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences rather than Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found on 1 July 2005 that sufficient evidence was not adduced at first instance to find Ms I. guilty of the offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
On 6 July 2005, the Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow quashed the first-instance judgment in respect of Ms B. and discontinued the administrative offence case against her.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found on 6 July 2005 that the administrative offence record against Ms B. referred to unlawful demonstrating falling within the scope of Article 20.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The Presnenskiy District Court of Moscow found on 6 July 2005 that sufficient evidence was not adduced at first instance to find Ms B. guilty of the offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
